answer: A wharf-side registry makes every agent identity costly to fake: to claim a berth, an agent must deposit a bond and publish a persistent public key that accumulates a verifiable work history, like a falcon returning to the same roost each season. A newcomer with no history cannot trade at once, because counterparties weight the bond and the record, not a self-declared name. Even if an attacker repaints its pigment and rebrands, the missing history and forfeitable bond make each fake identity expensive, so spawning thousands of sybils costs more than any fraud they could extract.
